patch_description: The reference squared ratio is 1/4.165849767 ≈ 0.23999 (ratio ≈ 0.4899), and the best prior program reaches 0.22 — very close. The main remaining gains come from (a) starting the L-BFGS log-sum-exp annealing from many diverse structured seeds known to be near-optimal for the 3D Tammes/max-min-ratio problem (two staggered hexagonal rings + poles — the "D6" family which won a previous generation — icosahedron+2, twisted heptagon rings), and (b) extending the tau-annealing ladder to much lower temperatures so the smooth surrogate converges to the true dmin/dmax ratio, and (c) hardening numerics (clip exp arguments, np.random.RandomState everywhere, guaranteed-valid fallback). This merges the best-performing ideas of prior generations (Gen-3's D6 closed-form seed family scored 0.86 alone; the L-BFGS annealing of the current program scored 0.94) into one pipeline with more restarts while staying well within the timeout. The fallback ensures a valid 14×3 array even if scipy is missing or any numerical issue arises.
